source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

41041.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Lincoln County gave Merkley (D) 15,526 votes to Smith's (R) 9,283, a Democratic margin of 24 points. Harris carried it by 18 points in 2024, so the county moved 6 points toward the Democrats, slightly more than Oregon's statewide shift of 5 points. It ranks 14th of 36 Oregon counties by move. Every county in the state moved left.

The county cast 25,915 votes, 87% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Counties of similar size and 2024 vote moved by comparable amounts: Clatsop and Deschutes each shifted 5 points and Lane 3. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

41007.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Clatsop County gave Merkley 11,224 votes to Smith's 7,989, a Democratic margin of 16 points, up from Harris's 11-point edge in 2024. That 5-point shift toward the Democrats matches the statewide move almost exactly, as Merkley carried Oregon by 19. It sits in the middle of the state's 36 counties, all of which moved left. Comparable counties moved in step: Deschutes and Lincoln by 5 and 6 points, Clackamas by 3. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left, so Clatsop's shift was modest by that measure.

The county cast 19,899 votes, 87% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41071.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Merkley and Smith, Yamhill County stayed Republican but by less: Smith carried it by about 1 point, 24,423 votes to 23,807, after Trump won it by 6 in 2024. That is a 5-point move toward the Democrats, matching both the statewide shift and the typical Oregon county. All 36 Oregon counties moved left. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points.

Turnout was 49,822, or 87% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Jackson and Wasco moved slightly more, about 6 points each, while Polk moved 3.

41013.t:
Crook County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, with Smith beating Merkley 10,107 to 3,445, a margin of 48 points. That is about 3 points narrower than Trump's 51-point win here in 2024. Every Oregon county moved toward the Democrats, but Crook moved less than most, ranking 31st of 36 against a typical shift of 5 points. Similar counties moved further: Baker 6 points, Malheur 6 and Morrow 9.

About 13,893 votes have been counted, roughly 87% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 88% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

41027.t:
Hood River County moved about 6 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, going from Harris's 36-point margin in 2024 to a 42-point win for Merkley over Smith, 7,809 votes to 3,119. That is a bit more than Oregon's 5-point shift and the typical county's 5 points, ranking 11th of 36 in a state where every county moved left. It is well short of the typical national move of 14 points. Among similar Democratic-leaning counties, it outpaced Benton (1 point) and Washington (3) and matched Lincoln (6).

About 11,303 votes were cast, 90% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41055.t:
Sherman County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved 4 points toward the Democrats. Smith carried it by 53 points, 762 votes to 225 for Merkley, after Trump won it by 57 points in 2024. About 97% of the expected vote is counted. Turnout was 1,015 votes, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Every Oregon county moved left. Sherman's shift was slightly smaller than the typical county's 5 points and below the statewide 5-point move. Similar small, heavily Republican neighbors moved by comparable amounts: Harney by 6 points, Grant by 6, and Wheeler by 3. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

41001.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Merkley and Smith, Baker County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 6 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 49 points in 2024; Smith won it by 43, 5,755 votes to 2,196. That shift is slightly larger than the typical Oregon county's 5-point move, where every county moved left, and well below the typical 14-point national move.

Turnout was 86% of the 2024 vote, 8,193 ballots against 9,523, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar Oregon counties, Baker moved less than Morrow (9 points) and Malheur (6), and more than Crook (3).

41005.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Clackamas County voted for Merkley over Smith by 13 points, 115,807 to 88,827, after backing Harris by 10 points in 2024. That 3-point move toward the Democrats was smaller than the statewide shift of 5 points and the typical Oregon county's 5. It ranks 29th of 36 counties, all of which moved left. Comparable counties moved more or about the same: Deschutes and Clatsop by 5 points each, Lane by 3. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

About 210,692 votes were cast, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell whether the shift came from voters changing their minds or from some staying home.

41049.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Morrow County stayed firmly Republican but moved 9 points toward the Democrats. Smith carried it 2,689 to 1,132 over Merkley, a margin of 39 points, down from Trump's 48-point win in 2024. That was the second-largest shift among Oregon's 36 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Oregon county moved 5 points, matching the statewide move. Comparably Republican Baker and Malheur each moved 6 points, and Crook moved 3. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points.

About 3,951 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Just under 95% of the expected vote is counted, so the numbers may still move.

41031.t:
Jefferson County stayed Republican in Oregon's U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. Smith (R) beat Merkley (D) 6,094 to 3,706, a margin of about 24 points, down from Trump's 30-point win over Harris. That 7-point shift toward the Democrats ranks fourth of Oregon's 36 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 5 points, as did the state. Comparable counties moved less: Josephine 5 points, Union 3 and Wallowa 1. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

About 10,119 votes were cast, 87% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41029.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Republican Smith carried Jackson County over Democrat Merkley by just 213 votes, 49,214 to 49,001, after Trump won it by 6 points in 2024. That 6-point shift toward the Democrats ranks seventh among Oregon's 36 counties, all of which moved left, and is a little larger than the typical Oregon county's 5 points, though well short of the 14-point typical move nationally. Similar counties varied: Marion moved 7 points and flipped to the Democrats, Yamhill moved 5 and Polk 3.

Turnout was 101,226 votes, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot show how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds rather than from who stayed home.

41057.t:
Tillamook County flipped in Oregon's U.S. Senate race, giving Merkley 7,148 votes to Smith's 6,803, a Democratic margin of about 2 points in a county Trump carried by 1 point in 2024. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats, a little less than the typical Oregon county's 5 and well short of the 14-point national norm. All 36 Oregon counties moved left. Comparable counties ranged from Polk's 3-point shift to Marion's 7.

So far 14,407 votes have been counted, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With about 89% of the expected vote in, these numbers may still move.

41063.t:
Wallowa County moved less toward the Democrats than any other county in Oregon in the U.S. Senate race between Merkley and Smith. Smith carried it 2,993 to 1,439, a Republican margin of 34 points, almost the same as Trump's 35-point win here in 2024. That one-point shift compares with a typical move of 5 points across Oregon, where all 36 counties moved left, and 14 points nationally.

Similar counties moved further: Union shifted 3 points toward the Democrats, while Umatilla and Jefferson each shifted 6 or 7. About 4,540 votes were cast, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41033.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Josephine County voted for Smith over Merkley by 24 points, 23,774 to 14,442, with 39,339 votes counted. That is about 5 points less Republican than its 29-point margin for Trump in 2024. Statewide, Merkley won by 19 points, and every one of Oregon's 36 counties moved toward the Democrats, the typical one by 5 points. Josephine ranked 16th. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Linn 4 points, Jefferson 7, Douglas 3.

Turnout was 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Only 91% of the expected vote is in, so these numbers may still move.

41061.t: Union County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, voting for Smith over Merkley by 38 points, 8,387 votes to 3,653. That is a 3-point shift toward the Democrats from Trump's 41-point margin over Harris in 2024. Every Oregon county moved left, and Union's shift was among the smallest, ranking 34th of 36. The typical Oregon county moved 5 points, as did the state, which Merkley won by 19. Similar counties moved further: Klamath by 5 points, Malheur and Umatilla by 6 each. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points. About 12,419 votes were cast, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41009.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Columbia County voted for Smith over Merkley by 8 points, 13,491 to 11,426. Trump carried it by 14 points in 2024, so the county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than the state's 5-point shift and the typical Oregon county's. All 36 Oregon counties moved left, and Columbia ranks 10th. Similar counties moved less: Curry by 4 points, Coos by 3 and Yamhill by 5. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left, well beyond Columbia's shift.

Turnout was 83% of the 2024 vote, with 25,927 ballots cast against 31,094, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41015.t:
Curry County backed Smith over Merkley in the U.S. Senate race by 6,424 votes to 4,979, a Republican margin of 12 points. That is 4 points better for the Democrats than Harris's 16-point deficit here in 2024, a smaller shift than Oregon's statewide 5-point move and the typical Oregon county's 5. All 36 Oregon counties moved left, and Curry ranks 23rd. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

The county cast 11,781 votes, 84% of its 2024 total of 14,018, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar Oregon counties, Columbia moved 6 points, Wasco moved 6 and flipped to a narrow Democratic edge, and Coos moved 3.

41035.t:
Klamath County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved about 5 points toward the Democrats. Smith (R) won 19,328 votes to Merkley's (D) 8,585, a margin of 37 points, down from Trump's 42-point win in 2024. That shift is close to Oregon's statewide move of 5 points and its typical county's, ranking 20th of 36 in a state where every county moved left. It is well below the national typical move of 14 points. Similar counties moved by different amounts: Umatilla 6 points, Union and Douglas 3 each.

Turnout fell to 28,726 votes, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

41019.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Douglas County gave Smith 33,674 votes to Merkley's 15,763, a Republican margin of 35 points. That is about 3 points closer than Trump's 38-point win here in 2024, a smaller shift than the statewide move of 5 points toward Merkley. Every Oregon county moved left, typically by about 5 points; Douglas ranks 32nd of 36. Among similar counties, Union moved by the same amount, while Umatilla (6 points) and Klamath (about 5) moved more.

Turnout was 84% of the 2024 vote, about 51,000 ballots against 60,756, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 92% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

41051.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Multnomah County voted for Democrat Merkley over Republican Smith by 67 points, 295,646 to 53,733. That is 5 points more Democratic than its 62-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024. The shift matches both Oregon's statewide move of 5 points and the typical Oregon county's, though it trails the typical 14-point move among counties nationwide. Merkley won the state by 19 points.

The county cast the most votes in Oregon, 362,595, but that is 89% of its 2024 total of 408,474. With turnout down, the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nearby Washington County moved 3 points and Hood River 6.

41003.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Benton County gave Merkley 29,511 votes to Smith's 12,008, a Democratic margin of 41 points, up from Harris's 40-point edge over Trump in 2024. That 1-point shift toward the Democrats ranks 35th of Oregon's 36 counties. Every county moved left, the typical one by 5 points, and the statewide margin moved 5 points. Comparable counties moved further: Hood River by 6 points, Washington and Lane by 3 each.

So far 43,038 votes have been counted, 87% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 88% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

41045.t:
Malheur County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, with Smith beating Merkley 6,041 to 2,624, a margin of 38 points. That is 6 points narrower than Trump's 44-point win over Harris in 2024, slightly more than Oregon's 5-point shift and enough to rank sixth among the state's 36 counties, all of which moved left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

About 8,966 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Baker moved about as much as Malheur, while Union and Klamath shifted less.

41069.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Merkley and Smith, Wheeler County stayed heavily Republican but moved about 3 points toward the Democrats. Smith led 528 to 195, a margin of 44 points, compared with Trump's 47-point margin in 2024. All 36 Oregon counties moved left, and Wheeler's shift was smaller than the typical county's 5 points, ranking 30th. Similar small, Republican counties moved more: Gilliam by 10 points, Morrow by 9 and Sherman by 4.

Wheeler cast the fewest votes of any Oregon county, 757, about 88% of its 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot show who changed their mind and who stayed home. About 95% of the expected vote is counted, so the numbers may still move.

41021.t:
Gilliam County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved more toward the Democrats than any other county in Oregon. Smith beat Merkley 647 to 302, a 35-point margin, down from Trump's 46-point win in 2024. That 10-point shift was about double the typical Oregon county's 5 points and the statewide 5-point move. It was still smaller than the typical 14-point move among counties counted nationally.

Turnout was 978 votes, 87% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar heavily Republican rural counties, Morrow moved 9 points, Malheur 6 and Wheeler 3.

41067.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Washington County, Oregon's second-largest by votes cast, gave Merkley 161,201 votes to Smith's 71,337, a Democratic margin of 37 points. Harris carried it by 34 in 2024, so the county moved 3 points toward the Democrats. That is less than the typical Oregon county's 5-point shift and well below the typical national move of 14. Every Oregon county moved left, and Washington ranks 25th of 36. Among similar counties, Lane also moved 3 points, Benton 1 and Hood River 6.

Only 85% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. Turnout so far is 82% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

41053.t:
Polk County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by less. Republican David Smith led Democrat Jeff Merkley 18,290 to 17,810, about 1 point, after Donald Trump carried it by 4 in 2024. That shift of about 3 points toward the Democrats ranks 33rd of Oregon's 36 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Oregon county moved 5 points, and nationally the typical move was 14. Similar neighbors moved further: Yamhill 5 points, Marion 7 and Tillamook 4.

Only 77% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 37,308 ballots counted so far equal 79% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

41017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Deschutes County voted for Democrat Merkley over Republican Smith by about 16 points, 60,642 to 44,014. That is a shift of about 5 points toward the Democrats from Harris's 10-point margin in 2024, close to the statewide move of 5 points and slightly above the typical Oregon county's 5. Every Oregon county moved left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points. Nearby comparisons varied: Clackamas moved 3 points, Clatsop 5 and Marion 7.

Turnout was 88% of the 2024 vote, 107,459 ballots so far, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 91% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

41043.t:
Linn County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. David Smith (R) beat Jeff Merkley (D) 35,927 to 23,423, a margin of 20 points, down from Trump's 24-point win over Harris. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats, slightly smaller than the typical Oregon county's 5 points and far below the 14-point typical move nationally. Every Oregon county moved left. Similar Republican counties moved by comparable amounts: Coos 3 points, Josephine 5 and Jefferson 7.

About 61,625 votes were cast, 87% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41047.t:
Marion County, which Donald Trump carried by 2 points in 2024, has so far voted for Jeff Merkley over David Smith in the U.S. Senate race, 48,767 to 43,639, a Democratic margin of 5 points. That is a 7-point move toward the Democrats, third-largest among Oregon's 36 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Oregon county moved 5 points, the state as a whole 5, and the typical county nationally 14. Similar counties moved less: Jackson 6 points, Yamhill 5 and Polk 3.

Only 65% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. The 95,126 votes tallied equal 61% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

41059.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Umatilla County voted for Republican Smith over Democrat Merkley, 16,408 to 8,325, a margin of 32 points. Trump carried the county by 38 points in 2024, so it moved 6 points toward the Democrats. That was a bit more than the typical Oregon county's 5-point shift and ninth-largest of the state's 36. Similar counties moved less: Douglas and Union by 3 points each, Klamath by 5. Merkley won statewide by 19.

The county cast 25,528 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, these numbers may still move.

41037.t:
Lake County stayed one of Oregon's most Republican places in the U.S. Senate race. Republican David Smith beat Democrat Jeff Merkley 2,825 to 628, a 62-point margin, compared with Trump's 65-point win in 2024. That 3-point shift toward the Democrats is smaller than the state's 5-point move and the typical Oregon county's 5. It is far below the typical 14-point move nationally. Lake ranks 27th of 36 Oregon counties by move, and all 36 shifted left.

Comparable Republican counties moved further: Grant by 6 points, Harney by 6 and Sherman by 4. Lake cast 3,539 votes, 86% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

41023.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Grant County voted for Republican David Smith over Democrat Jeff Merkley by 2,807 to 784, a margin of 55 points. That is 6 points less Republican than its 60-point margin for Trump in 2024, slightly more than the typical Oregon county's shift of 5 points and close to the state's own 5-point move. Every one of Oregon's 36 counties moved left, and Grant ranks 13th. Similar counties moved by similar amounts: Harney by 6 points, Sherman by 4 and Lake by 3.

About 3,700 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

41065.t:
Wasco County flipped in the U.S. Senate race, giving Merkley a narrow edge over Smith, 5,157 votes to 5,085, a Democratic margin of about 1 point. Trump carried the county by 6 points in 2024, so it moved 6 points toward the Democrats. That is a bit more than Oregon's typical county (5 points) and the fifth-largest move of the state's 36, though well short of the national typical move of 14. It is one of three Oregon counties to switch from Trump to the Democrat. Similar counties moved less: Tillamook 4 points, Yamhill 5, Polk 3.

Turnout was 81% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 89% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

41039.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Merkley and Smith, Lane County gave the Democrat 113,051 votes to 64,278, a margin of about 27 points. That is 3 points more Democratic than Harris's 23-point margin in 2024, a smaller shift than the 5-point move statewide and well short of the typical county nationally, which moved 14. Lane ranks 26th of Oregon's 36 counties by move, all of which moved left, and fourth by votes cast. Washington and Clackamas, two other large counties, moved by similar amounts.

About 183,811 votes were cast, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot show how much of the change came from voters switching sides and how much from voters staying home.

41011.t:
Coos County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. David Smith (R) beat Jeff Merkley (D) here 16,529 to 11,652, a margin of R+17, compared with Trump's R+20 over Harris. That 3-point shift toward the Democrats trails Oregon's 5-point statewide move and its typical county's 5 points, ranking 28th of the state's 36 counties, all of which moved left. Nearby counties of similar size and lean moved a bit more: Curry 4 points, Linn 4 and Columbia 6.

About 29,164 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

41025.t:
Harney County stayed heavily Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but less so than in 2024. David Smith beat Jeff Merkley 2,744 to 800, a margin of R+53, down from Donald Trump's R+59 over Kamala Harris. That is a move of 6 points toward the Democrats, slightly more than the typical Oregon county's 5 points and close to the statewide shift. It is well short of the national county median of 14.

The move was larger than in similar rural Republican counties nearby, such as Grant (6), Sherman (4) and Lake (3). About 3,652 votes were cast, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
